content: I just realize that Mathlib's definition of NoAtoms is that the measure of each singleton is zero. I think this is really nonstandard and different from definitions I learnt in the past (i.e. ∀ s, 0 < μ s → ∃ t ⊆ s, 0 < μ t ∧ μ t < μ s). May I know the initial motivation for the design? Shall we change this definition? I think we should introduce the definition of Atoms (a measurable set that has positive measure and contains no set of smaller positive measures) and then use this definition to define atomic/nonatomic measures.

Did some archeology and found it was introduced at https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/pull/3760. It has the comment "possibly should be redefined as ∀ s, 0 < μ s → ∃ t ⊆ s, 0 < μ t ∧ μ t < μ s." since the beginning and still has it as a TODO here

I think I'll make a PR in the next several days. If NoAtoms is used for measures with atoms, how should I name the original typeclass for measures such that each singleton has measure zero? Maybe NullSingletonClass (as an extension of MeasurableSingletonClass)?

I have recently run into the same issue (a proof requires the stronger, standard notion of nonatomic measure as opposed to the current mathlib version). Are you still planning to update the mathlib definition soon, @Yongxi Lin (Aaron) ?
Otherwise I'd be happy to pick it up and give it a try.

I didn’t start this project yet, so feel free to refactor it if you’d like. Once you submitted a PR you can post your PR number here and I can try my best to give you some comments.

If NoAtoms is to be replaced by the correct definition, can we completely remove the current one? It seems to be instantiated exclusively for measures that would also be non-atomic under the new definition.
:search: MeasureTheory.Measure.restrict.instNoAtoms, MeasureTheory.NoAtoms.mk, and 14 more

Lua Viana Reis said:

If NoAtoms is to be replaced by the correct definition, can we completely remove the current one? It seems to be instantiated exclusively for measures that would also be non-atomic under the new definition.

I think we should keep the old definition. The current definition of NoAtoms in Mathlib is sometimes referred as continuous measures in the literature. See for example page 106 in Folland's real analysis book.

This notion is also sometimes used in probability (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singular_distribution).
Then it should be called that instead, probably?

What about NoExtendedAtoms? Continuous has a lot of meanings (one may think of measures with density wrt Lebesgue, for instance), while extended atoms can only refer to sets that are measurably atoms, i.e., contain no set of strictly smaller measure.

@Sébastien Gouëzel are you suggesting to keep the name docs#MeasureTheory.NoAtoms as-is and use NoExtendedAtoms for the stronger notion discussed in this thread?

I believe NoAtoms (or Atomless or Nonatomic) is usually used for the stronger notion:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(measure_theory)

Of course, we can keep the current notion around, and I agree that the name continuous is ambiguous. How about NoSingletonAtoms or NullSingletonClass (sugggested by Aaron)?
I'm not interacting much with this part of the library so my opinion is not super relevant, but NullSingletonClass sounds good to me.
Of course I expect that both notions cross-reference each other
I like NoAtoms (or one of the variations) for the stronger notion and NullSingletonClass for the weaker one.
